summary.headline: Orders and revenue fell WoW and landed behind target in the first week of 2026, though both remain well ahead of last year.

points.what: Orders came in at 681, down 5.7% from 722 the week before, while revenue fell 6.1% to $47,322.
points.so_what: Both measures sit close to the 8-week averages of 680 orders and $49,398, so the week was a step back rather than a break in the recent range.

points.what: Orders reached 87.4% of the weekly target and revenue 87.5%, a revenue shortfall of $6,736.
points.so_what: The quarter opens behind target, with next week's bar higher at 810 orders and $58,234 of revenue.

points.what: Orders grew 51.3% and revenue 48.9% versus the same week last year.
points.so_what: Both are good YoY results but below the 75% growth the 2026 targets assume, which is why the week fell short of target.

points.what: New signups rose 12.5% to 252 while the cancellation rate edged up to 16.0%, its third consecutive rise.
points.so_what: Customer acquisition strengthened in the week even as order quality weakened, so the two should be read together.

points.what: The cancellation rate has risen three weeks in a row, from 13.0% to 16.0%.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $563 of weekly revenue, so the streak carries a real revenue cost.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 15 Dec 2025 rose 1.6 pp to 10.3%, above the 1.0 pp notable threshold and 3.2 pp higher than last year.
points.so_what: This is a bad move in customer returns, and the two most recent weeks are still too young to report.

points.what: AOV of $82.73 was flat WoW but sits outside its 8-week range and is 3.2% below last year at $85.44.
points.so_what: With AOV no longer contributing, revenue growth depends on order volume, which fell this week.

points.what: Weekly orders hit 87.4% of target (681 versus 779, a gap of 98 orders) and weekly revenue 87.5% ($47,322 versus $54,058).
points.so_what: The year starts behind target on both measures, and next week's targets step up to 810 orders and $58,234.

points.what: QTD revenue is at 87.5% of target, leaving $727,233 of the $774,555 full-quarter target to earn in the 12 remaining weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter needs a faster pace than week 1 delivered to close the gap.

points.what: YTD attainment is 87.5%, and the $3,888,802 full-year target requires $73,875 of revenue per week versus the recent 8-week run-rate of $49,177.
points.so_what: At the current pace the full-year target is out of reach, so the size of the required step-up is the key number to watch.

points.what: North America drove the decline with 33 fewer orders, 80.5% of the total change, falling 20.2% to 130 orders.
points.so_what: The WoW drop is concentrated in one region rather than spread across the business.

points.what: Search accounted for 92.7% of the change with 38 fewer orders, down 7.2% to 487, while Organic added 12 orders (up 13.6% to 100).
points.so_what: Search holds 71.5% of orders, so its direction sets the direction of the weekly total.

points.what: LATAM was the only region to grow, up 4.2% to 99 orders, and it also led YoY growth at 70.7%.
points.so_what: LATAM is the only region growing above the 75%-style pace the targets assume, but at 14.5% of orders it cannot offset North America.

points.what: AOV was $82.73, essentially unchanged from $82.76 last week but down 3.2% from $85.44 a year ago.
points.so_what: The YoY decline is assessed as bad and means revenue is growing more slowly than orders.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 0.3 pp to 16.0%, the third rise in a row from 13.0%, though it remains 1.3 pp below last year's 17.3%.
points.so_what: At roughly $563 of revenue per percentage point, the direction matters even while the YoY comparison is favourable.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 15 Dec 2025 was 10.3%, up 1.6 pp on the prior week and up 3.2 pp YoY.
points.so_what: This refers to the mature week only, as orders from the two most recent weeks have not had the full 14 days to be returned.

points.what: New signups rose 12.5% WoW to 252 and 10.5% YoY, while orders fell 5.7% WoW and rose 51.3% YoY.
points.so_what: Customer growth moved in the opposite direction to orders this week, and its YoY pace is well below the order growth rate.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
